expected_mechanism: LQR receives saturated command at switch; recovery depends on remaining lateral error and curvature.
Prolonged positive saturation at apex overwhelms LQR integral action; state error grows past recoverable region.
Negative saturation at exit; LQR may recover if error small, fail if error large due to opposite curvature.
Strong negative saturation at high speed exit; LQR cannot counteract combined speed curvature and clamp.
Solver failure during straight; LQR must immediately stabilize with zero curvature assumption.
Extended solver failure entering curve; LQR recovery viability depends on error state at switch instant.
Short solver failure at high-speed exit; LQR may recover if error was small pre-failure.
Constant bias added to steering; LQR feedforward may compensate if bias small relative to gain.
Large bias at apex overwhelms LQR; recovery fails as command saturates and error diverges.
Drift rate applied at entry; LQR may track if rate slow enough for error correction between switches.
Fast drift at high speed exit; LQR integral action insufficient, error diverges past recovery boundary.
Stale command repetition; LQR sees same steering output, may mistake for valid command or detect mismatch.
Prolonged stale command at apex; LQR gain scheduled to speed may diverge if command lags curvature change.
2-tick output delay; LQR receives delayed command, switch timing may miss recovery window.
6-tick delay at high speed exit; LQR command outdated, recovery fails due to state mismatch.
